title: Medicaid eligibility-error correction exists, but federal oversight does not yet learn consistently which fixes work
source_unit: GAO-26-108017 review of Medicaid eligibility errors, state corrective action plans, and CMS oversight
geography: United States; all 50 states and the District of Columbia for error reporting, with seven selected states reviewed for corrective actions

observations.period: Medicaid reporting years 2014-2025; corrective-action review 2019-2024; report published August 18, 2026 and publicly released September 17, 2026

denominator.unit: selected states whose corrective-action plans and state-level evidence GAO reviewed

national_reporting_scope.unit: states plus the District of Columbia covered by Medicaid eligibility-error reporting

state_corrective_actions.unit: types of corrective actions used by selected states to reduce identified eligibility errors

cms_oversight_gap.value: CMS feedback did not ensure that state corrective-action plans consistently included all required elements

cross_state_learning_gap.value: CMS did not consistently analyze errors and corrective actions across states and years to determine effectiveness or transferability

access_boundary.value: the report identifies error-correction and oversight stages, not individual coverage restoration or continuity
access_boundary.unit: evidence boundary between administrative correction and usable benefit access

observations.method: GAO reviewed national Medicaid eligibility-error reports, state-level reports from a rotational review system, corrective-action plans from seven selected states for 2019-2024, CMS feedback and communications, and interviews with CMS and state officials.
observations.uncertainty: The selected-state review is not a national estimate of corrective-action quality. Eligibility-error rates and corrective actions do not show which applicants lost or retained coverage, how quickly errors were corrected, or whether beneficiary health, time, trust, or household costs changed.
observations.subgroup: Medicaid applicants and enrollees, state eligibility agencies, CMS oversight staff, eligibility systems, and corrective-action categories; state program design, reporting year, error type, and administrative capacity vary.
observations.counterinterpretation: Variation in corrective-action plans may reflect legitimate state flexibility, differing error types, or data limitations rather than uniformly weak oversight. Training or system updates may reduce errors even when cross-state evaluation is incomplete; a documented oversight gap does not prove that each state correction failed.

related_sources.claim: GAO landing page identifies the report and recommendations.

boundary: This record establishes a Medicaid eligibility-error, state-correction, and federal-learning boundary. It does not establish individual coverage loss or restoration, procedural-denial rates, health outcomes, beneficiary trust, household burden, or the causal effectiveness of any particular corrective action.
